Why does this keep happening? I'll tell you why. Because we trust abstractions we have never read! So I did what any stubborn programmer would do — I tore the whole thing down and **rewrote it from scratch**.

And the result? A lean, mean random generator — two hundred lines of pure, battle-tested C. Picture this: it's 2 a.m., the coffee is cold, and my random generator has just crashed — again.

Here's the thing: the random generator doesn't have to be complicated. You just have to respect it. The lesson? Never underestimate the power of simple code. Trust me, you'll thank yourself later.
